title: Ephemeral preview + canary rollout orchestration for private deployments
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational draft for running ephemeral preview clusters (per-PR or per-branch) in customer-like VPC/on-prem environments and safely promoting those artifacts through a canary promotion flow backed by Argo (ArgoCD + Argo Rollouts). The goal is to provide a consistent, automated path from CI build -> signed artifact -> mirrored registry -> pinned release -> gradual promotion with automated observability gates, while keeping the Terraform-managed infra reproducible and reversible.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not prescribe a single bucket for secrets; secrets integration will be implementation-specific per customer (KMS/HSM or vault).
- Not an exhaustive security audit for airgapped installs; separate compliance checklist exists.

Terminology (quick):
- preview-cluster: a short-lived k8s namespace/cluster that mirrors customer config for a single PR or branch.
- artifact-promote: the act of copying a signed OCI artifact from ephemeral to stable mirror and pinning its digest in the release repo.
- release-pin: version/digest recorded in Terraform/Helm values that Argo follows.
- redwood-signer-proxy: lightweight internal signing service that interacts with customer KMS/HSM and Cosign-like flow.

High-level flow:
1) CI builds image -> unit/integration tests run.
2) CI publishes unsigned image to build registry (internal CI registry), triggers signing job.
3) Signer service (redwood-signer-proxy) requests signature using customer-backed key (HSM/KMS agent). Signed manifest appended.
4) Signed image is mirrored into the customer mirror registry (mirror.example.corp) with immutability enabled.
5) CI creates a preview release: deploy to ephemeral preview-cluster using Helm chart values patched by CI. Argo Application for preview clusters is created via Terraform workspace.
6) Automated smoke tests & small synthetic load run in preview cluster.
7) If tests pass, artifact-promote job copies the image into the stable mirror namespace (promote.example.corp) and writes a release-pin entry to the release repo (gitops). The PR includes the helm values update (image.digest).
8) ArgoCD picks up the release repo change; Argo Rollouts triggers canary rollout to production-ish fleet per the configured policy.
9) Observability gates watch latency/5xx/error budget and alert on regression; automated rollback if thresholds met.

Terraform module notes (pattern & interfaces):
- Module: private-deploy/preview-cluster
  inputs: cluster_id, customer_vpc_id, namespace_prefix, ephemeral_ttl (string), node_pool_size (number), provider_creds_ref
  outputs: cluster_endpoint, kubeconfig_secret_name, argocd_application_name
  intent: create an isolated namespace or dedicated ephemeral cluster depending on customer profile. Use ephemeral_ttl to drive automated cleanup lambda/job.

- Module: private-deploy/registry-mirror
  inputs: upstream_registry, mirror_registry, immutability_policy (bool), s3_backend_prefix, signer_service_endpoint
  outputs: mirror_host, repository_prefix
  notes: module must enable digest-only writes and set retention rules. For airgapped customers, module wires an OCI proxy that supports blob caching and pull-through.

- Module: private-deploy/gitops-repo-sync
  inputs: git_remote, deploy_branch, protected_files_list, signing_key_ref
  outputs: webhook_secret_name
  notes: this module provisions the minimal IAM and webhooks for CI to push release pins into the repo. Use a short-lived push user for CI.

Helm chart / umbrella patterns (best practices):
- Ship an umbrella chart at infra/charts/redwood-ingress-umbrella that contains:
  - core service charts as dependencies (api, router, worker)
  - a tiny values overlay per environment (preview, staging, prod)
- Keep image and digest under top-level values.app.image:
  values.yaml example:
  image:
    repository: mirror.example.corp/redwood/api
    tag: "v0.0.0-pr-123"
    digest: "sha256:..."
- CI should prefer setting image.digest instead of tag when promoting to release branch. Helm values in gitops repo should be the single source of truth for pinning.
- Avoid chart templating that reads outside values (no reading of external configmaps at render time). Keep templating deterministic for diffs.

ArgoCD + Argo Rollouts strategy snippets:
- Preview clusters: ArgoCD Application created per-PR using autogenerated app name: redwood-preview-<pr>-<shortsha>. Application source points to infra/overlays/previews/<pr>/values.yaml.
- Production: single Argo Application per service pointing at infra/overlays/prod/values.yaml. Promotion is achieved by updating the values.yaml in infra/overlays/prod with new image.digest.
- Rollout policy (canary):
  - steps: 10% for 10m -> 50% for 15m -> 100%
  - analysis: custom MetricProvider scraping via PrometheusAdapter with these checks:
    - request_latency_p95 < baseline*1.25
    - error_rate_5m < baseline+0.5%
    - cpu_throughput does not spike > 2x
  - automated_abort: if any analysis step fails, rollback to previous stable revision.

Image promotion & signing choreography (practical):
- Build job: produces image: registry.ci.redwood/svc:pr-123-<shortsha>
- Sign job: POST to redwood-signer-proxy with artifact reference, principal. Proxy invokes customer's KMS agent to sign and returns signed manifest. Signed image is pushed to mirror (mirror.example.corp/svc@sha256:...).
- Promote job (post-approval): copy digest to stable mirror namespace and create release-pin commit which updates infra/overlays/prod/values.yaml with the digest. CI creates a signed git commit using repository signing key.

Key rotation choreography (recommended safe path):
1) Provision new key in KMS/HSM with limited lifetime and mark as secondary on signer service.
2) Re-sign a small set of canary images to confirm the signer-service secondary key path works.
3) Mirror new signatures to mirror registry.
4) Gradually switch signer service primary to new key and monitor for signature verification failures in staging.
5) If any verification errors occur, roll back signer primary to previous key and open incident.

Observability signals & thresholds (implementation detail):
- Primary signals: p95 latency, 5xx rate, overall error budget burn (SLI), readiness probe failures, pod restart count.
- Synthetic checks to run in preview cluster: health endpoint, simple end-to-end workflow, background job that verifies KV/cache performance.
- Alerting: immediate page if 5xx spike > 1% absolute over baseline for 5 minutes during canary. Minor alerts for higher latency increases.

Preflight checks and smoke tests (examples):
- k8s sanity: kubectl --kubeconfig ${KUBECONFIG} get nodes && kubectl get pods -n preview-123 -o wide
- Helm dry-run with pinned digest: helm upgrade --install svc ./svc-chart --namespace preview-123 --values pr-values.yaml --set image.digest=sha256:... --dry-run
- Smoke curl checks against preview ingress and internal service endpoints.

Rollback playbook (runbook style):
- Automated rollback: Argo Rollouts reverts to previous stable replicaSet and marks rollout as aborted. Alert on #incident channel.
- Manual immediate rollback steps: 1) Lock gitops repo branch (prevent CI pushes), 2) revert release-pin commit via git revert, 3) push to repo and wait for ArgoCD sync, 4) verify production health.
- Postmortem: capture timeline, failed metric, implicated images, signer logs, and terraform diffs. Attach to JIRA ticket.

Ephemeral cleanup & cost control:
- preview-cluster module must create a TTL controller that deletes resources beyond ephemeral_ttl.
- CI must call terraform destroy or mark workspace for deletion after merge. Automation should reclaim unreferenced EBS/volumes within 24h.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Single ephemeral cluster vs many namespaces: namespaces are cheaper but introduce noisy-neighbor risks for kernels and GPU.
- Do we run real customer VPC networking in preview clusters or mock via overlay? Running real networks increases fidelity but also blast radius.
- Signing key model for offline/airgapped: decide if signer-proxy should run inside customer network or as a sealed remote agent that only exchanges attestation tokens.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- [ ] Prototype preview-cluster terraform module with ephemeral_ttl and argocd integration (owner: Diego) - ETA 2 weeks.
- [ ] Implement a minimal redwood-signer-proxy PoC that supports HSM-backed cosign flow (owner: Priya) - ETA 3 weeks.
- [ ] Add canary analysis queries to observability catalog and test them in staging (owner: Marta) - ETA 1 week.

References and helpful commands:
- GitHub PR pattern: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/432 (example release-pin PR)
- Useful local commands:
  export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/preview-pr-123
  helm upgrade --install svc ./charts/svc -n preview-pr-123 --values ./ci/pr-values.yaml --set image.digest=sha256:...
  kubectl -n preview-pr-123 rollout status deploy/svc --timeout=5m
- Related JIRA: ENG-1245, ENG-1301 (signer key rotation)

Notes: This is a working draft intended to capture the current preferred flow. Implementation details will vary by customer (airgapped vs VPC) and will need a short integration checklist per deployment. Encourage teams to comment in the PR and link test artifacts produced by the prototype PoC.
